note: Generated from the web engine. Do not hand-edit. Regenerate with: cd web && CRUCIBLE_WRITE_GOLDEN=1 npx vitest run golden-particle

scenarios.name: burst-settles-under-gravity
scenarios.why: The simplest scene: a hundred bodies thrown from one point, then gravity, air friction and the bouncing walls. No attractors and no springs, so a failure here is in the integrator itself and nowhere else.

scenarios.name: burst-charges-repel
scenarios.why: The same burst with the electrostatic force turned up hard. Under 300 bodies the engine switches to comparing every pair, so this exercises that whole path, including the rule that a pinned body is pushed by charge but never moved.

scenarios.name: galaxy-orbits-hold
scenarios.why: A black hole with 300 bodies in Keplerian orbit. The most sensitive scenario in the set: orbital motion amplifies any arithmetic difference, so if sine and cosine were even one bit apart between the engines this is where it would show.

scenarios.name: galaxy-event-horizon-reemission
scenarios.why: A tight world, so bodies fall into the hole and are re-emitted — either into a fresh orbit or, one time in seven, as a jet. That branch draws from the random stream, so it pins down both the re-emission maths and the draw accounting.

scenarios.name: waterfall-recycles-at-the-floor
scenarios.why: Bodies that reach the floor are teleported back to the top with fresh random velocity. Three draws per recycled body per frame, so the counts only agree if the recycle condition triggers on exactly the same bodies on the same frames.

scenarios.name: shockwave-expands-and-bounces
scenarios.why: A ring driven outward into the walls simultaneously. Every body hits a boundary on nearly the same frame, which is the worst case for the bounce code.

scenarios.name: blackhole-with-wrapping-edges
scenarios.why: Wrapping boundaries combined with an attractor. Wrapping is a true modulo rather than a single correction, which matters exactly here: near a black hole bodies can move more than a world-width in one frame.

scenarios.name: double-vortex-two-attractors
scenarios.why: Two black holes, with bodies assigned alternately and given opposite spin. Confirms attractors are accumulated rather than the nearest one winning.

scenarios.name: repulsor-pushes-outward
scenarios.why: The repulsor branch, which is the only one that subtracts its force.

scenarios.name: solar-flare-lifespans-recycle
scenarios.why: Every body has a lifespan and an origin, so they expire and are reborn continuously. Each rebirth draws twice, and the origin sits mid-world so it takes the ordinary rebirth path rather than the fountain one.

scenarios.name: cosmic-fountain-rebirth-at-the-floor
scenarios.why: The other rebirth path: an origin within 50 of the floor is treated as a fountain and gets a different, upward velocity drawn from three more numbers. Both paths have to be covered or half the rebirth code is untested.

scenarios.name: quantum-lattice-holds-its-shape
scenarios.why: The only preset with a restoring pull toward each body's origin. Also the regression guard for that pull being gated on an explicit flag: it used to be inferred from having an origin, ignoring gravity and being charged, which also described seven orbital presets and crushed them inward.

scenarios.name: dna-helix-wraps-and-undulates
scenarios.why: The helix wave and its horizontal wrap. Guards the strand being an explicit property rather than inferred from the body's colour — which broke permanently the moment any tool repainted it.

scenarios.name: dna-helix-repainted-stays-in-the-helix
scenarios.why: The same helix with the painter held over it, which recolours every body under the cursor. Before the strand became a property this silently dropped repainted bodies out of the wave for good, so this scenario is the regression itself.

scenarios.name: synchrotron-between-two-wells
scenarios.why: Two offset attractors with a dense ring, which produces frequent close passes.

scenarios.name: pour-fluid-mode
scenarios.why: Turns on the fluid flag, which no other scenario in this set exercises.

scenarios.name: flock-boids-cohere
scenarios.why: The flocking pass: cohesion, alignment and separation over up to 360 bodies. Separation is divided by distance, so closer neighbours push harder — it used to accumulate the raw offset, which made avoidance weaker the closer they got.

scenarios.name: nbody-mutual-gravity
scenarios.why: Mutual attraction between every pair, with no central body to dominate it.

scenarios.name: cloth-hangs-from-pinned-corners
scenarios.why: A spring lattice with pinned top nodes. Springs index into the body list, so this is where an off-by-one in that indexing shows up as a sheared sheet.

scenarios.name: cloth-on-a-canvas-too-narrow
scenarios.why: A cloth wider than the world, so the computed gap collapses. Guards the rule that a rest length of zero does not disable every spring — which it used to, leaving the sheet as loose beads.

scenarios.name: rope-swings-from-a-pin
scenarios.why: A chain of springs from a single pinned end. The clearest test of spring order.

scenarios.name: blob-holds-volume
scenarios.why: A ring of springs plus long cross-braces, so each body has several springs pulling in conflicting directions.

scenarios.name: mouse-attract-sweeps-through
scenarios.why: The attract force, with the cursor crossing the scene so the falloff is swept.

scenarios.name: mouse-repel-and-release
scenarios.why: Repulsion held for part of the run and then released, so the frames after release prove the force stops being applied rather than lingering.

scenarios.name: mouse-vortex-swirls
scenarios.why: The vortex force, which is tangential with a small radial component.

scenarios.name: mouse-gravity-well-swirls-inward
scenarios.why: The strongest of the cursor forces, and the only other one with a swirl term.

scenarios.name: mouse-freeze-damps
scenarios.why: Freeze multiplies velocity by 0.7 and applies no force, so it must only slow.

scenarios.name: mouse-hyper-drive-recolours
scenarios.why: Hyper-drive applies a large fixed push and repaints permanently. The push ignores the falloff, which makes it the one mode that can exceed the speed limit and so the best test of the clamp.

scenarios.name: mouse-hawk-pushes-hard
scenarios.why: Hawk repels the bodies but attracts the swarm at more than double force — the one mode that means opposite things to the two halves of the field.

scenarios.name: mouse-emitter-spawns-continuously
scenarios.why: Emitter adds six bodies per frame at the cursor, each drawing four times. The count grows every frame, so this is also the test that the cap evicts the oldest through the path that keeps springs valid.

scenarios.name: void-boundary-removes-escapees
scenarios.why: Void boundaries delete anything that leaves, shrinking the list mid-tick. Removal renumbers every later body, so this is where a stale index would surface.

scenarios.name: decay-speed-counts-down
scenarios.why: A global decay rate gives a lifespan to bodies that had none. Stopped partway through, so the recorded lifespans show the countdown itself rather than only its end state.

scenarios.name: decay-speed-empties-the-field
scenarios.why: The same scene run past the deadline. Without an origin these expire and are removed rather than reborn, which is the other half of the lifespan code, and the removal happens mid-tick while the force loop is still iterating.

scenarios.name: speed-limit-clamps-everything
scenarios.why: A deliberately tiny speed limit. Guards the clamp applying to every body: it used to sit inside the branch for orbital bodies, leaving ordinary ones completely uncapped despite the interface offering one global limit.

scenarios.name: trails-off-above-the-threshold
scenarios.why: Trails are only recorded up to a thousand bodies, and a stale trail is discarded the moment recording stops. Trails do not affect physics, so this is checked via the recorded trail lengths rather than the positions.

scenarios.name: swarm-alone
scenarios.why: A large batch goes to the swarm, which is a separate parallel-friendly store with its own integrator and spatial-hash collisions. No object bodies at all, so the swarm's tick is isolated.

scenarios.name: swarm-with-cursor-and-wrapping
scenarios.why: The swarm under an attracting cursor with wrapping edges. The swarm only understands pull and push, so every cursor mode has to map onto one or be ignored — painter and freeze used to blow it outward instead.

scenarios.name: swarm-and-bodies-together
scenarios.why: Both halves of the field at once, sharing one random stream and one set of limits. The whole-field cap is why the swarm's budget subtracts the bodies already present.

scenarios.name: well-placed-into-a-scene
scenarios.why: A draggable well added on top of an existing scene, rather than by a preset.
